check: whether Test-S5Release's jar selection actually picks the main artifact, checking the logic against the real files rather than reading it
why: The comparison at the end of that script decides reproducibility from whichever jar it selects first. If the exclusion were wrong it would hash the sources jar, and the comparison would still produce a stable answer - the wrong one - because sources jars are reproducible too. Reading the filter is weaker than running it against the two files that exist.
theFilter: name matching plaincraft-great-wall-*.jar, excluding *-sources.jar and *-dev.jar, then sorted by name and the first taken

whatRunningItGives.isItTheMainJar: Yes - the sources jar is excluded rather than merely sorted after
whatRunningItGives.matchesDeployedJar: Yes, identical to the 80506fe5... SHA recorded as deployed, so the selection reaches the artifact under test

whyTheExclusionMattersMoreThanItLooks: Both jars would hash consistently across two builds, so a wrong selection would not fail - it would report a match between two sources jars. That is a check that always passes, which is the shape this session has flagged twice elsewhere.
aMethodNote: I mistyped a log pattern in the status check this round, writing 'task' where the message says 'tick'. Both returned zero, but only by coincidence - so I ran a positive control on the scan, confirming it finds STRESS_REFILL 40 times, Can't keep up 651 times and GreatWall 87 times. The zero is a real zero.
